name: Time Structuring
oneLine: Berne's six ways people fill time together - withdrawal, ritual, pastime, activity, game, intimacy - running roughly from least to most intense and risky stroking.
whatYouDid: You toured a party and sorted six different corners into their actual time-structure - the bookshelf pastime, Troy's doorway ritual, Camellia's kitchen activity, Dev fishing for a game, Priya's intimacy on the balcony - all happening within the same twenty minutes.
confusion: People mix up pastime and game because both can look like "just talking"; the tell is the payoff - a pastime ends when people are done chatting, a game ends with both people feeling bad after a sudden, unexpected switch.

fromBook.quote: there are six different ways in which they can spend their time

expand.definition: The six time structures, in order of roughly increasing stroke intensity and perceived risk: withdrawal (self-strokes only), ritual (fixed, predictable exchange), pastime (familiar talk, no commitment to act), activity (goal-directed work), game (ulterior transactions ending in bad feelings), intimacy (authentic, uncensored exchange).
expand.otherFraming: Steiner frames the same list as driven by structure-hunger - the need to optimally structure time in social situations for the procurement of a maximum number of strokes.
expand.tryThisToday: For one conversation today, notice which of the six you're in - and whether it's the one you actually want to be in.
